name: Epoxy chunk
description: A broken lump of hard cast epoxy. Stock for patching or moulding plastic parts.
notes: 62 by 50 mm and 32 mm high: a cast lump with flat moulded faces, stepped to a fracture face and a darker mould ridge. resin-honey is the nearest finish for cured epoxy. It brings no quality; its use is as a recipe input.

name: 40 mm filter port
description: A threaded clear plastic housing that takes a 40 mm screw-on filter and seals it to a gas mask.
notes: 45 mm across the flange and 30 mm tall: clear body, four thread ridges, a steel retaining ring round the spigot and a dark bore painted flush. The box is large because the flange overhangs the barrel.

name: Inhalation valve
description: A small one-way valve that lets filtered air into a gas mask. A rubber flap sits on a plastic seat.
notes: 35 mm across and 13 mm tall with its snap spigot. The box is large because it is a ring round a thin flap. rubber-gum is the amber valve flap, plastic-matte-black the seat.

name: Stretch fabric patch
description: A square of stretchy synthetic fabric cut from sportswear. Strong and flexible, for sewing close-fitting clothes.
notes: A 152 mm square lying loose and rippled, 2 mm thick. The item size is the folded patch. Name drops the trademark. lycra-blue picked so it reads apart from the red synthetic patch.

name: Synthetic fabric patch
description: A square of woven synthetic fabric. It does not rot.
notes: A 152 mm square lying flat with one corner curled up 26 mm, 2 mm thick. The item size is the folded patch. nylon-red is a plain synthetic colour; other colours can recolour body and fold.

name: Panoramic lens
description: A curved strip of tough clear polycarbonate, the single wide lens of a full-face mask or visor.
notes: A 3 mm strip 64 mm tall bent to a 100 mm radius stands round air. The 170 mm length is measured round the curve, so the chord is 156 mm. Dark mounting tabs at each end. Tiles draw plastic-clear opaque; it stays see-through in game.

name: Plastic chunk
description: A broken piece of moulded plastic, still ribbed on one side. Stock for making or mending plastic things.
notes: A 75 by 55 mm fragment of a crate wall with a cross rib and a corner wall stub, 26 mm high. The variants ride here as the brief asks, but a gasket, a stopcock, a test tube rack and a microcentrifuge tube tray are distinct objects; each deserves its own model and draft in a later batch.

name: Large plastic sheet
description: A large sheet of thin polythene, folded. Keeps rain off, wraps things or makes a clean surface to work on.
notes: Folded into a 280 by 220 mm pad 24 mm thick with its loose end lying over the top and onto the floor. work_surface is a new quality name; level 1 because Deadvox has no scale for it yet. plastic-frosted is the nearest milky polythene.

name: Plastic sheet
description: A sheet cut from a bin bag. Useful for waterproofing clothes.
notes: A 300 by 240 mm piece lying crumpled, up to 32 mm high. The item size is the sheet balled up. plastic-bag renders mid-grey.

name: Polycarbonate chunk
description: A thick offcut of clear, tough polycarbonate with one corner snapped off.
notes: 70 by 50 by 12 mm. The fracture face is plastic-frosted. Tiles draw plastic-clear opaque.

name: Rigid plastic sheet
description: A large stiff sheet of clear polycarbonate, still in its protective film.
notes: 1.22 m square and 8 mm thick; a frosted film covers the top with one corner peeled back. The film and the folded corner add height. Too large for any pocket: the size is a placeholder for an item carried in the hands.

name: Thermoplastic resin chunk
description: A melted and hardened blob of tough off-white plastic that softens again with heat. For making or mending parts.
notes: 64 mm across and 28 mm high, a rounded blob with a lobe and a drip run off it so it reads melted rather than cast or cut. plastic-white sets it apart from the honey epoxy and clear polycarbonate chunks.
